licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These ten buckets cover the distinct clusters visible in the data: fraud/deceit in obtaining a license, negligence/incompetence/misconduct in practice, criminal convictions, improper use of the professional seal/signature, aiding unlicensed practitioners, substance abuse or physical/mental impairment, false advertising or misrepresentation in practice, reciprocal discipline from other jurisdictions, catch-all statutory/rule/order violations, and financial conflicts of interest or improper compensation—each capturing a meaningfully different disciplinary rationale with few items left without a natural home.

profession_specific.exempt_building_type.rationale: These nine buckets capture the dominant clusters in the data: single-family homes (the most common exemption), small multifamily dwellings (2–16 units), farm/ranch buildings, small commercial/industrial/storage buildings (by size, cost, or occupancy thresholds), minor alterations and repairs that don't affect structure or safety, accessory/outbuildings ancillary to residences or farms, preengineered or prefabricated buildings, owner-built structures for personal use, and a residual catch-all for uncommon items like signs, teaching, or federal government work.
